text: When you build an image, most of what ends up inside it isn't your code. It's your base OS packages, your language runtime, and every third-party dependency your project pulls in, often several layers deep through transitive dependencies you never directly declared. A vulnerability can enter through any layer in that stack, which is exactly why image scanning exists — you simply cannot track every package's CVE status by hand.

Known vulnerabilities are catalogued as CVEs in public databases, with the National Vulnerability Database as the central one, alongside advisories from Debian, GitHub, npm, and PyPI. Each CVE carries a CVSS score and a severity bucket — critical, high, medium, or low — and a scanner's job is to fingerprint every package in your image and match it against exactly those published disclosures.

Running trivy image against a tag walks every layer, lists every package it recognizes, and reports each matching CVE with its severity and fixed version if one exists. Docker ships a comparable built-in tool, Docker Scout, using docker scout cves — different engine, same underlying question.

A scan nobody reads doesn't stop anything, so the real value is running it in CI and failing the build on serious findings. Limiting the severity to critical and high, setting a non-zero exit code, and ignoring CVEs with no available fix yet keeps the gate meaningful instead of noisy.

Separate from today's findings is the SBOM — the software bill of materials — a complete inventory of every package and version in the image, generated by tools like syft in a standard format such as CycloneDX. Having that inventory on hand means you can answer whether you're affected the instant a new CVE is published, without re-pulling anything.

Scanning turns a vague worry about unknown vulnerabilities into a concrete, automatable gate in your pipeline, run on every build rather than checked occasionally by hand. Next, we'll look at what happens once code is already running inside the container — and how to make sure it isn't running as root.
